# My plan for this year

Let me think through it. I've been working this land for 45 years, ever since I was a young man. My wife passed a few years back and the children are in the city now, so it's just me on these 18.8 mu. I can't do what I used to — my back doesn't like bending over cotton rows the way it did at 40 — but I know this land and I know what it gives me.

**How I split the land.** I keep 6 mu in cotton and the other 12.8 mu in wheat-maize double cropping. I used to do more cotton, but picking it alone at my age is too much. Six mu I can manage if I hire two women from the next village for a few weeks in the fall. The wheat-maize is steady — food on the table, a bit to sell, and the cycle is something my hands know in their sleep.

**Wheat (12.8 mu).** I plant around October 10th, right after the maize comes off. The custom operator from the village drills it for me — 30 yuan per mu, worth every fen because I can't walk behind a seeder anymore. I put down one bag of compound fertilizer before planting, about 50 jin per mu, and then when the wheat greens up in March I spread half a bag of urea, maybe 20-25 jin. That's how I've always done it and I get around 450 kg per mu in a normal year. My neighbor Old Wang splits the urea into two doses but I've never bothered — mine grows fine. I irrigate before the freeze if November is dry, then at green-up, then jointing, and one more near grain filling if the sky doesn't do it for me. The well is metered so I don't waste.

**Maize (12.8 mu, same ground).** Right after the wheat combine comes off in June I get the planter in the next day — you cannot wait, the window is a week if you're lucky. Compound fertilizer in the row with the seed, then urea topdress at the big bell stage, about 25 jin. Water once after planting to get the stand up. If July is hot and dry I water again at tasseling, but usually the summer rain helps me out. Maize is the easy one. I get 500 kg per mu most years.

**Cotton (6 mu).** I planted mid-late April — this year April was cool so I waited till the 20th. Cotton eats fertilizer and it needs spraying, so I spend more per mu here than on grain. I apply compound fertilizer at planting, urea at flowering, and potash helps the bolls. I spray for aphids and bollworm two or three times — you cannot skip it, a bollworm year wipes you out. I irrigate twice, at bud stage and again when the bolls are setting. Picking is the hard part — I hire two women for about three weeks and pay them around 1,200-1,500 yuan total. Still, when the cotton sells, that's the real cash in the year.

**What I hold back.** I keep some money in the drawer for emergencies — a bad rain at wheat harvest, a pest flare in cotton, or my knee giving out. At my age and on my own, I do not gamble with what I don't have.
